title: The Choir of Harrow Glen
premise: Folklorist Astrid Almeida arrives in Harrow Glen to record a carol the villagers sing only once, at dusk, and never repeat. Her overnight audio captures a second voice answering her questions while she sleeps — a voice that knows things only the dead of Harrow Glen should know. As she investigates, she discovers the village has been feeding it identities for generations, and that her own recordings have invited it to wear hers. In the final hours before sunrise, Astrid must choose between erasing every trace of herself — voice, name, memory — or letting the choir complete its song with her as its newest member; she survives by giving it the one thing no villager ever offered: someone willing to listen all the way through.
about_author: J. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories in remote coastal villages before turning to fiction. They write horror about what recordings keep after the speakers are gone.

chapters.title: The Song Sung Once
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She arrives in fog-bound Harrow Glen, welcomed too warmly by innkeeper Maren Hale, and records the dusk carol from the churchyard — noting how villagers scatter the moment it ends. That night she plays it back and hears a second voice beneath the melody, answering questions she never asked aloud. Emotional beat: scholarly fascination curdling into unease.

chapters.title: What the Tape Remembers
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Reviewing her sleep recordings, she hears the second voice using her own timbre, reciting details of her childhood she never told anyone. The vicar, Elias Thorn, warns her to leave before 'the counting' — but reveals the village has been surrendering names to the thing for two centuries. Emotional beat: dread deepening into complicity as she realizes her documentation is an invitation.

chapters.title: The Counting
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, fraying into the entity's interjections. At midnight the village locks its doors and the choir begins again without throats. Astrid, trapped in the church, confronts the voice wearing her memories and learns the truth: it doesn't steal identities — it collects the unfinished, the unheard, and the villagers have always abandoned their dead mid-song. Climactic beat: terror transfigured into terrible understanding.

chapters.title: Until Sunrise
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, steady now. Holding out until dawn, she does what no one has done: listens to the whole song, answers every question, gives the entity the completion it was starved of. At first light the voice releases her — leaving one recording that plays a harmony no living throat made. Resolution beat: grief and found family, as the village finally mourns aloud together.
